title: Benefits, Growth & Role Mapping Playbook
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook explains how Redwood links benefits, role ladders, and onboarding tooling to help new and existing employees navigate compensation, career progression, and access to people systems. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, ICs preparing for promotion, and new hires.

Purpose

- Make benefit enrollment and changes discoverable and actionable.
- Provide a clear, measurable promotion rubric that ties to role expectations.
- Describe the tooling and operational steps required for onboarding, benefits enrollment, and role-change workflows.

Scope

Applies to: all full-time employees, contractors on 6+ month engagements, and hiring managers across engineering, product, and GTM. Excludes one-off contingent workers and external consultants (handled by procurement).

Ownership and escalation

- Document owner: People Ops (owner_team).
- Operational support: HR Benefits Specialist (people-ops-benefits@redwood.ai).
- Escalation path: People Ops -> VP People -> Legal (for policy/legal exceptions).

Quick links (systems referenced)

- HRIS: Workday (enrollment, life events)
- ATS: Greenhouse (hiring workflows)
- SSO/Provisioning: Okta (app access)
- Payroll & equity: ADP + Carta
- Docs & runbooks: Confluence (this space)
- Benefits vendor portal: vendor.redwood-health.example (single-sign-on)

How to use this playbook

1. If you are a new hire: follow the Onboarding Checklist below.
2. If you are a manager: complete the Manager readiness steps and follow the hiring flow.
3. If you are preparing for promotion: review the Promotion Rubric and collect evidence as shown in the Promotion Evidence template.

Section A — Benefits navigation (practical guide)

Intro: Redwood offers a core benefits package plus elective programs that vary by geography. The steps below are operational instructions for signing up, changing coverage, and handling life events.

1) Common benefits (US example)

- Health: medical (multiple carrier options), dental (Delta Dental), vision (VSP).
- Financial: 401(k) with employer match, pre-tax commuter benefits, HSA (where available).
- Time off: unlimited PTO policy (manager-aligned), parental leave (primary/secondary), caregiver leave.
- Wellness & perks: mental health stipend, home office allowance, professional development budget.

2) Enrollment steps (new hire or qualifying life event)

- Within 7 days of start: log into Workday -> "Benefits" -> start enrollment.
- Select plans and confirm beneficiaries.
- Submit enrollment and check vendor portal to verify provider acceptance (expected within 5 business days).
- If a life event occurs: open a life-event case in Workday within 30 days and upload supporting docs.

3) Common exceptions and who to contact

- Specialist: benefits-ops@redwood.ai for vendor mismatches or late enrollments.
- Payroll issues: payroll@redwood.ai.

Section B — Role ladders and promotion rubric

Overview: Career progression at Redwood follows an impact-based ladder with explicit signals for breadth, depth, and leadership. Promotions are driven by demonstrated outcomes and calibrated via manager+peer review.

Promotion dimensions (same for IC and manager tracks):

- Impact: measurable product or revenue outcomes tied to work.
- Scope: size and complexity of systems, teams, or projects led.
- Craft: technical or domain skill mastery and quality of work.
- Autonomy: ability to set approach and unblock others.
- Influence & leadership: mentoring, cross-functional collaboration, and strategic input.

Level mapping (quick reference table)

| Level | Typical title | Experience (yrs) | Key signals |
|-------|---------------|------------------:|------------|
| L2 | IC2 / Associate | 0–2 | Delivers assigned work with quality; asks for feedback; ships features with tests |
| L3 | IC3 / Engineer | 2–5 | Owns features end-to-end; reduces defects; contributes to team design |
| L4 | Senior / Staff | 5–9 | Leads cross-team initiatives; mentors others; owns a critical service or component |
| L5 | Principal / Senior Staff | 8+ | Shapes product/tech direction; drives large-scale changes; recognized mentor and domain expert |

Promotion process (high level)

1. Initiation: Manager or IC submits a promotion packet in Workday/PeopleOps portal including the candidate's self-assessment, manager assessment, and 3–5 evidence artifacts (PR links, metrics dashboards, customer feedback).
2. Calibration: People Ops convenes the calibration panel (manager, peer reviewer, business partner).
3. Decision: Panel makes recommend/refer/deny. For recommend, HR issues the promotion effective date and compensation adjustments.
4. Post-promotion: Update title in HRIS, GitHub display name, and Confluence profile.

Promotion evidence checklist (recommended artifacts)

- Release notes or PRs showing technical ownership.
- Post-release metrics (latency, error rate improvements, adoption).
- Mentorship / onboarding docs authored.
- Cross-functional project plans and outcomes.

Section C — Onboarding: first 6 months (practical timeline)

Week 0 (pre-boarding)

- Manager: complete hiring checklist in Greenhouse and verify offer acceptance.
- People Ops: send Welcome packet (Workday invite, benefits link, IT form).
- IT: create Okta user and request access provisioning template.

Week 1 (orientation)

- Day 1: join Welcome session, meet manager, complete benefits enrollment (if applicable).
- End of week: 1:1 with buddy and review 30/60/90 plan.

Month 1 (ramp)

- Deliver a scoped onboarding task (small bugfix or doc).
- Complete required security training and Confluence tour (track completion in LMS).

Month 2–3 (ownership)

- Lead a small feature or internal improvement.
- Schedule a formal feedback checkpoint with manager at 60 days.

Months 4–6 (impact)

- Take ownership of a cross-team deliverable.
- People Ops: 6-month career sync to discuss role progression and development plan.

Tooling checklist (actions managers or ICs must complete)

- Okta: ensure apps assigned (Slack, GMail, GitHub, Jira, Confluence).
- GitHub: add to org team and repo ACLs.
- GCP/AWS: provision least-privilege roles via infra-team template.
- PagerDuty: confirm on-call rotation access for SRE hires.
- LMS: assign security and compliance courses.

CLI / Sample admin step (examples for infra owners)

- GitHub team grant (example):
  curl -u admin:$(okta token) -X PUT "https://api.github.com/orgs/redwood/teams/{team_slug}/memberships/{username}"

Section D — Hiring & manager checklist (fast path to time-to-impact)

Manager pre-hire tasks

1. Create role brief: include expected impact in first 6 months, level, compensation range, and interview rubric.
2. Get budget approval and post in Greenhouse.
3. Align interview panel and send calibration guide (use the Interview Guide template).

Interview flow (recommended)

- Phone screen (30m): recruiter + culture fit.
- Technical loop (2–3 interviews): problem solving, system design, role-specific exercise.
- Hiring committee review: committee approves and finalizes compensation.

Offer & acceptance (steps)

1. Recruiter prepares offer in Greenhouse; manager confirms compensation.
2. Offer sent; candidate responds within 72 hours.
3. People Ops initiates onboarding and pre-boarding workflows.

Section E — Compensation & benefits alignment (how decisions are made)

- Compensation bands are set annually by People Ops with input from Finance and market data.
- Promotions include base and, where warranted, bonus/equity adjustments.
- Managers should discuss total compensation (base + bonus + equity + benefits) during calibration and at offer.

Section F — Templates and artifacts (where to find them)

- Promotion packet template: Confluence -> /templates/promotion-packet
- Manager hiring checklist: Confluence -> /templates/manager-hiring-checklist
- Onboarding 30/60/90 template: Confluence -> /templates/30-60-90
- Troubleshooting: People Ops runbook for late benefits enrollments -> /runbooks/benefits-late-enroll

Section G — Examples and edge-cases (realistic scenarios)

- Scenario: International hire with delayed visa start date
  1) People Ops sets a provisional start in Workday.
  2) Benefits enrollment is queued and confirmed once start date is finalized.

- Scenario: Fast promotion requested (urgent customer need)
  1) Manager submits an expedited promotion packet with quantitative results.
  2) People Ops convenes an expedited calibration. Decision timeline: target 7 business days.

FAQ

Q: How long does benefits enrollment take to show in payroll?
A: Typically one full payroll cycle after enrollment is submitted; contact payroll@redwood.ai for exceptions.

Q: Who approves equity grants on promotion?
A: Compensation team + Finance must sign off for equity above the level of standard promotion bands.

Appendix: contacts and SLAs

- People Ops response SLA: 48 business hours for standard inquiries.
- Benefits escalations: 24 business hours for vendor mismatches.
- Payroll: 72 business hours for payroll corrections.

Related pages and next steps

- See competency and rotation maps for role-specific expectations (/confluence/company-handbook/02_roles-and-career/competency-maps-and-rotation-paths-2027).
- Managers: complete the Calibration Playbook once per promotion cycle (Q1 & Q3 recommended).

End of playbook.
